edges.description: Lower-lobe pulmonary consolidation and alveolar-interstitial inflammation manifest clinically and radiographically as atypical pneumonia.
Systemic pro-inflammatory cytokine release during acute psittacosis drives high fever.
Lower respiratory tract inflammation elicits cough.
Alveolar and bronchial exudation in psittacosis pneumonia frequently produces sputum expectoration alongside cough.
Pulmonary consolidation and impaired gas exchange cause dyspnea.
Systemic febrile illness in psittacosis frequently produces prominent headache.
Acute systemic inflammatory response during psittacosis onset causes chills.
Systemic inflammation and acute febrile illness cause prominent fatigue.
Systemic cytokine release and skeletal muscle involvement produce myalgia.
Uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation in severe psittacosis progresses to diffuse alveolar injury and acute respiratory distress syndrome.
Dysregulated systemic host response in severe psittacosis pneumonia progresses to sepsis.
Fulminant systemic psittacosis can progress to vasopressor-dependent septic shock.
Extrapulmonary systemic inflammation and severe febrile illness cause acute neurocognitive disturbance manifesting as delirium.
Systemic dissemination and inflammatory hepatotoxicity cause hepatic dysfunction with elevated circulating transaminases (such as AST).
Acute-phase systemic inflammation and hepatic dysfunction produce hypoalbuminemia.
Severe multisystem psittacosis causes renal impairment.
Severe systemic chlamydial infection and inflammation can cause acute myocardial injury.
Acute systemic infection and inflammatory redistribution cause peripheral lymphopenia despite normal or mildly elevated total leukocyte counts.
Acute innate inflammatory response produces peripheral neutrophilia alongside normal or mildly elevated total leukocyte counts.
Systemic acute-phase inflammatory signaling markedly elevates circulating C-reactive protein.
Acute-phase reactant synthesis during systemic psittacosis elevates the erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
Skeletal muscle injury during multisystem psittacosis elevates circulating creatine kinase activity.
Pulmonary and systemic cellular injury in severe psittacosis elevates circulating lactate dehydrogenase.
Systemic inflammation and microvascular fibrin turnover in severe psittacosis elevate circulating D-dimer levels.

nodes.description: C. psittaci depends on its bacterial 70S ribosome for protein synthesis. Doxycycline, a tetracycline with good intracellular bioavailability, binds the decoding center on the 30S ribosomal subunit to prevent aminoacyl-tRNA binding at the A site and arrest bacterial translation (while macrolides bind near the nascent peptide exit tunnel on the 50S subunit) — combining the ribosomal target with the intracellular penetration needed to reach the organism, which is why a tetracycline rather than a beta-lactam is first-line.

evidence.reference_title: Ribosome-Targeting Antibiotics: Modes of Action, Mechanisms of Resistance, and Implications for Drug Design.
evidence.snippet: The decoding center (DC) is the region comprising the A site on the 30S subunit that monitors the correct base pairing between the mRNA codon and the anticodon of the aa-tRNA.

evidence.reference_title: Ribosome-Targeting Antibiotics: Modes of Action, Mechanisms of Resistance, and Implications for Drug Design.
evidence.snippet: Tetracyclines inhibit translation by preventing binding of aa-tRNA to the A site (35), while the smaller molecule negamycin stabilizes tRNA binding in the A site, inhibiting translocation and stimulating miscoding (36).

evidence.reference_title: Ribosome-Targeting Antibiotics: Modes of Action, Mechanisms of Resistance, and Implications for Drug Design.
evidence.snippet: The majority of antibiotics that bind to the 50S subunit cluster at the PTC, where the peptide bond formation occurs, and within the nascent peptide exit tunnel (NPET) (Figure 1d).

nodes.description: Psittacosis follows inhalation of aerosols from infected birds. Chlamydia psittaci is an obligate intracellular bacterium that replicates within host cells via a biphasic elementary-body to reticulate-body cycle, an intracellular lifestyle that underlies intrinsic beta-lactam resistance and the requirement for cell-penetrant antibiotics.
